citation.description: Ticket description documents root cause with 200 in-suite samples showing cancel at 0.300-0.303 s, and freeze reproduction (SIGSTOP/SIGCONT) failing 3 of 3 runs at 4.63-4.66 s. Ticket comment attests: 'Before: a scratch pytest plugin that SIGSTOPs the test process 0.1 s into the call phase and SIGCONTs it 4.5 s later failed the unmodified test 3 of 3 on py3.11.16 with assert cancelled passing and assert elapsed < 4.5 failing at 4.63-4.66 s.'

criteria.criterion: The cause of the >4 s elapsed time is identified with a reproduction: the freeze reproduction fails the unmodified test 3 of 3 runs with `assert cancelled` passing, and the in-suite samples show the cancel landing 0.300-0.303 s after tool start.

The test no longer fails for that cause, without loosening its proof that the async tool is cancelled before its 5 s sleep completes: under the same 4.5 s freeze on py3.11 both tests pass 3 of 3 runs, and the tool test still asserts `cancelled` plus a `RetryPromptPart` for `slow` naming the 0.3 s timeout.
`test_stalled_server_trips_read_timeout_under_run_sync` asserts the `ReadTimeout` against a server that cannot respond before the client aborts, with no wall-clock ceiling.

citation.description: Ticket comment attests: 'Mutations: dropping tool_timeout=0.3 fails assert cancelled; read=5 with the server releasing at 1 s fails the ReadTimeout assert; restored file passes. py3.11 -n 4 3 of 3 pass.'

criteria.criterion: Each mutation check in Testing turns its test red, and the restored test is green.

citation.description: Ticket comment attests: 'make lint exit 0 (wall-clock-asserts clean); make typecheck exit 0.'

criteria.criterion: Bug 'test_tool_timeout_cancels_an_async_tool exceeds its 4.5s bound under CI load' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
